en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Investigation: 5.
The Question on Arising from Existence and Formations (Bhava-saṅkhāra-jāyamāna-pañha)
The King said:
“Venerable Nāgasena, are there any conditioned phenomena that arise without having previously existed?
“There are no such conditioned phenomena, Great King, that arise without having previously existed; rather, Great King, it is only those conditioned phenomena that already exist which arise.”
“Make a simile.
“What do you think, Great King? Was this house, where you are sitting, born without having previously existed?
“There is nothing here, venerable sir, that was born without having previously existed; only what already existed was born. Indeed, venerable sir, these...”
“The timber was in the forest, and this clay was on the earth;
through the appropriate effort of women and men, this house was thus produced.
“In the same way, Great King, there are no conditioned phenomena that arise without having previously existed; only conditioned phenomena that have already existed arise.”
“Give me another simile. “Just as, Great King,
whatever seeds and plants are sown in the earth, gradually attaining growth,
increase, and abundance, would yield flowers and fruits— yet those trees did not exist previously...”

“Just as those trees, O king, are born only from what has already come to be, so too, great king, there are no formations that are born from what has not come to be; those formations are born only from what has already come to be.
“Give me a further simile,” he said.
“Just as, great king, a potter takes clay from the earth and fashions various vessels, and those vessels do not arise without having existed, but arise only after having existed;
even so, great king, there are no conditioned phenomena that arise without having existed—conditioned phenomena arise only after having existed.
“Give me a further simile,” he said.
“Great King, suppose a lute had no soundboard, no skin, no hollow body, no neck, no plectrum,
no strings, and no bridge, and furthermore, there were no corresponding effort on the part of a person— would a sound be produced?
“Certainly not, Bhante.”
“But when, great king, there is the wooden body of a lute, the leather, the hollow body, the neck, the plectrum, the strings, the bow, and the appropriate effort of a person, would sound be produced?
“Yes, venerable sir, it would be produced.
“In the same way, great king, there are no formations that arise without having been; rather, only formations that have come to be arise.”
“Give me a further simile,” [the king said].
“Suppose, great king, there were no fire-drill wood, no fire-drill handle, no fire-drill cord, no upper fire-drill, no rag for tinder, and no human effort directed toward it—would fire be produced?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.”

"But when, great king, there is the fire-drill, there is the fire-drill base, there is the fire-drill cord, there is the upper fire-drill, there is the cloth, and there is the appropriate effort of a man, would that fire be produced?
"Yes, venerable sir, it would be produced.
"In the same way, great king, there are no formations that are produced without having existed; rather, formations are produced only after they have existed."
“Give me another simile.
“Suppose, great king, there were no gem, no heat, and no cow-dung; could fire be produced?
“No, venerable sir.”
“But when, great king, there is a gem, there is sunlight, and there is cow-dung, would fire be produced?”—

“Yes, venerable sir, it would be produced.”— “In the same way, great king, there are no formations that are produced without having come to be; rather, it is only when they have come to be that formations are produced.”
“Give me another simile.
“Suppose, great king, there were no mirror, no light, and no face—would a self be produced?
“Certainly not, venerable sir.”
“But, great king, if there were a mirror, if there were light, and if there were a face,
would a self be produced?”— “Yes, venerable sir, it would be produced.”—
“In the same way, great king, there are no formations that are produced without having previously existed; rather, only formations that have come to be are produced.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!
This was the fifth question, concerning that which is born of volitional formations.
